A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a small number of stimulated neurons is sufficient to generate the complex saccade properties of the SC population, and that the resulting E saccades are determined by a simple weighted summation of the single site contributions.

the network mechanism is able to account for most of the experimental data on the SC microstimulation, and thus may serve as a useful tool for the interpretation of SC microstimulation results in the future.

the spiking neural network mechanism for SC microstimulation is able to account for a wide range of saccade kinematics, and that it is a good candidate for explaining the saccade generation in the SC.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the SC population can be seen as a vectorial saccadic pulse generator that can produce a weighted average of its saccade properties in response to simultaneous stimulation of multiple sites in the SC.
a simple network model can explain many experimental results on microstimulation of the SC, and that the network properties are in good accordance with the known anatomy and physiology of the SC.
double stimulation in the network model produces the same E saccade properties as seen in single cell recordings, and that this is due to the same mechanisms as those underlying single stimulation.
